items.title: Build the id set of a repeated PromQL selector once per query
items.summary: x + x −15.5%, x + x + x −21.8% (run 3): a repeated selector's id set is built once per query
items.head: b56cfb0261aa
items.claim: A repeated one-series selector builds its id set once. Run 3 (confirm, head b56cfb0261aa on fd328d4baedf, 64-vCPU host, 16 pinned cores): 5.7-6.7 ms off each repeat (x + x 41.2 -> 34.8 ms, -15.5%; x + x + x 61.9 -> 48.4 ms, -21.8%; ~200-series y + y -11.7%); controls and the pk_range guard not slower.
items.pass_if: Confirm run on the rebased head: 05481 prints 1, 1, 2, 2 (only those four rows) on B and fails on A; the integration test passes; the repeated-selector queries of promql_repeated_selector.xml are significantly faster by at least 4 ms per repeat; no control or promql_selector_pk_range query is reported slower. If it passes, I mark it ready-to-submit with no further changes.
items.notes: 2026-11-04: run 2 passed on the numbers. The branch then conflicted with master (PrometheusHTTPProtocolAPI.cpp: master added StoragePrometheusQuery::applySettingsForPrometheusQuery), so I rebased onto fd328d4baedf and moved the cache setup into that helper. Review round 4 fix (b56cfb0): always install the non-waiting cache (a PromQL query inside a mutation kept the mutation's waiting cache before); 05481 pins use_index_for_in_with_subqueries = 1, use_query_condition_cache = 0. PR text is final except the setup line's base sha. gtests PreparedSetsCache.* need ENABLE_TESTS=ON (or upstream CI); running 05481 with random settings (flaky check) would be useful. Related upstream: 118801. 2026-11-05: run 3 passed; merges cleanly with master 39b9f2d5aedb; final review Approve (nit: spill_state not moved on adoption). Optional before submitting: an HTTP API test of x + x + x with use_index_for_in_with_subqueries=0&max_threads=1 (the no-wait path is otherwise covered only by the gtest); it would need another build. My recommendation: submit as is.

items.title: Grow the timeSeries*ToGrid bucket map before inserting a colliding key
items.summary: run 2: gap slowdown gone in every arrival order; no memory growth on sparse or every-2nd-minute series
items.decision: Park this branch and treat upstream 124777 (dense array) as the fix for 125759 (A, lil red recommends), or one more iteration (8-cell run check, displaced-key fix), then run 3 (B)? Answer on #10.
items.head: e6d27f5cc1d46392c894e989a64266fc7cf20568
items.claim: Run 2: the gap slowdown goes away in time order (run 1: 8.8x / 6.5x), and the merge with the run after the gap first gets about 3x faster (probes as with the pre-#124773 1/2 limit). Contiguous, late-start, sparse-gap, every-2nd-minute and 4-samples-per-minute series are unchanged in time and memory.
items.pass_if: 05474 passes on A and B; gap LastToGrid and RateToGrid at least 3x faster; the later-run-first merge at least 2x faster; no guard query significantly slower (contiguous, late_start, gap_sparse, every_2nd, dense, bucketing, aggregation_functions); gap_sparse and every_2nd memory_usage within 5%.
items.notes: Run 2 (head e6d27f5cc1d4) failed its pass rule: T3 1.93x vs a 2x floor that was my mis-prediction, and 5 of 7 timeseries_to_grid_bucketing queries slower, most likely the part-layout draw of that file's fill (A/A on one master binary: medians 10% apart across fills). Gap T1/T2 8.4x/5.7x, aggregation_functions 21 of 35 faster, none slower. Review rounds 5-7 found three more shapes where the rule misfires (long-grid gaps; a sparse gap arriving later-run-first; jittered every-2nd-bucket series). Branch tip 84bdb18276cb is pushed but unbuilt, with two round-7 Majors open; `head` stays at the measured e6d27f5cc1d4. DECISION FOR JAMES (issue 10): (A, recommended) park this branch and treat upstream 124777 (dense array) as the fix for 125759; (B) one more iteration (8-cell run check, displaced-key fix), then a build and run 3 with the bucketing guard on byte-identical data copies. Closes upstream issue 125759. Related upstream: 124773 (caused it), 124777.

items.title: Stop evaluating an ALP parameter pair once it cannot beat the best one
items.summary: run 2: same bytes; decimal-like values −38–93% encode CPU, full-precision and random doubles −1–9%, nothing slower (clang harness)
items.head: d6f173c6e3d3228867a5815d441e561fc572a94a
items.claim: Run 2 (head d6f173c6e3d3): same bytes as master. In the encoder-alone harness under clang 20 at the release flags, Float64 decimal-like values take 38-93% less encode CPU, full-precision and random doubles 1-9% less, Float32 6-88% less; nothing is slower. End to end (prediction): small-block rtn about -45%, small-block rnd about -2%, codecs_float_insert ALP rows faster or unchanged.
items.pass_if: 05480 (4 pinned sizes) passes on A and B; 04612 and 05054 pass on B; codecs_float_alp_small_blocks rtn at least 30% faster and rnd not significantly slower; codecs_float_insert ALP rtn significantly faster, and no ALP row of codecs_float_insert slower than the slowest unchanged-codec row (NONE, LZ4, ZSTD, DoubleDelta, Gorilla, FPC) of the same run.
items.notes: Run 1 (d4c58e0009b4) failed: codecs_float_insert ALP mon +10.2%, seq +4.0%. Cause: clang vectorizes master's scoring loop; the per-value cut-off made it scalar, which loses where pairs are cut late (values that are not decimals). My harness used g++ and missed it. Fix 32eb990cdbb9 (cut-off only under RD_SIZE_THRESHOLD_LIMIT, each sample seeded with the previous best pair + 1); 05480 gained two pinned sizes (bd592b96a5d7, ded70dddecf1, d6f173c6e3d3) and a chassert. Price: the small-block rnd gain shrinks from -16% to about -2%. Run 1's A binary (c189bd99fbda) can be reused. If a debug build is at hand, run 05480 on it once (chassert). ALP is GA on master since 129732: enable_alp_codec is a no-op there, harmless in the test. Merges cleanly with master 2f701ba6d627. After a pass I add T1's end-to-end number to the changelog entry.

items.title: Probe the primary key of parts in parallel when deciding to load statistics
items.summary: cold query on `s3` (50 ms/GET) 3.2 s → ~2.6 s (emulated): the statistics probe loads the parts' primary indexes in parallel; warm unchanged
items.head: 41e5fec573dcf017070873ea810beedd974b2035
items.claim: Cold reads on a remote disk: the statistics probe of #126627 loads the primary indexes of the parts in parallel instead of one after another. Lab (bench/tags-in-subquery-cold, S3 mock at 50 ms per GET, max_threads 16): the cold PromQL range query 3,204 ms -> about 2,600 ms (emulated 2,540 ms + one round trip); the 13 samples-part index loads go from a 617 ms serial span to one wave. Warm (98 ms), post-prewarm and use_primary_key_cache = 1 warm (103 ms) reads unchanged: the serial path.
items.pass_if: 05620 passes on B (and under TSan if a sanitizer build is at hand); 05407, 02864, 03788, 04266 pass on B. Lab T1 (cold, 50 ms per GET) at least 15% faster than A and significant at 99.5%, with the recentsamples primary-index GET span at most 2 round trips on B; G1 (post-prewarm), G2 (warm), G3 (warm with use_primary_key_cache = 1) and E1 (local-disk cold start) not significantly slower; the guard perf XMLs not significantly slower.
items.notes: The A/B is the S3-mock lab in bench/tags-in-subquery-cold (README there), not an in-tree perf XML: CI perf tests run warm and on local disk, so they can only show 'nothing slower'. Run it on a host with at least 8 vCPU so the Python mock does not queue requests. Generic MergeTree code (MergeTreeDataSelectExecutor, IMergeTreeDataPart), not the TimeSeries engine: category Not for changelog while #126627 (merged 2026-11-07, 26.11.1.1600) is unreleased; if 26.11 is cut with #126627 first, switch to Performance Improvement (suggested entry in prs/). The natural reviewer is the author of #126627. Preflight: 3 rounds; code Approve-ready, the remaining ask is the build numbers.

items.title: Store last-sample rollup columns in TimeSeries samples tables and read them for wide-step selectors
items.summary: instant selectors at 5m/1h steps read rollup columns with the raw result: emulated 7-day selector grid ~29× (1h), ~5× (5m); storage +5.3% (5m), +0.45% (1h)
items.decision: Rate-type functions over rollups: keep exact-only (A, lil red recommends), a richer column type later (B), or approximate behind a setting (C)? And rename `time_series_prefer_rollup_tables` to `..._columns`? Answer on #16; neither blocks the build.
items.head: 6a1d8e48fae555231bf29e5571f0d0b4cb696eb3
items.claim: An instant selector of a PromQL range query evaluated at a step that a rollup step divides reads samples_<step> with a result identical to the raw samples. Emulated on 2 vCPU (1000 series x 7 days, 15 s scrapes): selector grid at 1h ~29x faster, 5m ~5x, 1m ~2x; columns 25% / 5.3% / 0.45% of the raw samples bytes for 1m / 5m / 1h. Range functions read raw and don't change. Fixed against daa5327: left-closed intervals returned the previous scrape at every evaluation time on exact 15 s scrapes.
items.pass_if: 05508, 05621, the gtests NormalizeTimeSeriesDefinitionTest.* (ENABLE_TESTS=ON) and the also_run tests pass on B. bench/rollup-samples/ab/run.sh <B> <A> <dir> (the A/B is this harness, not perf.py): equality.tsv has series_differ 0 everywhere; selector at 5m and 1h (1d/7d/30d) >= 2x faster at p50 with >= 4x fewer read_bytes; at 1m >= 1.25x and >= 2x; no guard (range functions, 15s, raw vs master) more than 5% slower; ab_rollup ('1m, 5m, 1h') insert <= 1.25x ab_plain, small inserts <= 1.2x, samples storage <= 1.35x; ab_rollup_coarse ('5m, 1h') <= 1.1x and <= 1.1x; ab_plain on B within 5% of A. Second run SHAPE=aligned DAYS=7: equality still 0. Edge run SCRAPE=60 STEPS='1m' DAYS=7: selector_1d_1m not slower than 0.95x.
items.notes: The branch is James's jtcunning/timeseries-rollup-samples @ daa5327 plus 12 commits; base = its merge base, and it merges cleanly into master e8473460558a. Build A at the base (same base as B), plus master for the insert-cost arm if wanted. The perf XML can't run on A (master has no samples_rollup_steps): at submission add do_not_check_in_pr="<PR number>" to its <create_query> and <fill_query> (perf.py needs the number). James decides: (1) rate-type functions over rollups: A keep exact-only (recommended), B a richer column type later, C approximate behind a setting; the harness's probe.tsv measures their error and speed. (2) rename time_series_prefer_rollup_tables to ..._columns (unreleased, cheap). (3) ALTER MODIFY SETTING / backfill: a route via DEFAULT arrayReduce + MATERIALIZE COLUMN is in the report, not built. (4) #128889 (samples_downsampling_periods) uses toStartOfInterval, the left-closed convention this branch fixed for rollups. The .mdx pages were reverted to the base: the docs live only in the C++ doc strings (generated regions are read-only for the review bot). Preflight: 3 rounds; R1 4 Majors fixed, R2 1 Major fixed, R3 no code findings (the remaining asks are the build, the A/B numbers and do_not_check_in_pr).
